title: Yang Guifei

image.credit: Shōhaku Art Museum, Japan; via arthistoryproject.com

altText: A tall Japanese painting on silk of a woman in layered, richly patterned robes, painted in soft, delicate colors with fine, flowing lines.

source.verifiedBy: arthistoryproject.com artwork page text (title, year, medium, public-domain statement)

context: A painting in opaque watercolor on silk by Uemura Shōen, dated 1922 and held by the Shōhaku Art Museum in Japan. Its source page tags it as bijin-ga, the Japanese tradition of pictures of beautiful women, and the title names Yang Guifei, a famous woman of Tang-dynasty China.

descriptions.k: A woman in long, pretty robes. The painting is very big and soft. Look at her clothes. Which colors do you see? What do you think she is doing?
descriptions.g12: Uemura Shōen painted this woman on silk, a smooth cloth, with soft watercolors. Her robes are full of patterns and gentle colors. The lines are thin and neat. What small details in her clothes can you find?
descriptions.g35: Uemura Shōen made Yang Guifei in 1922 using opaque watercolor on silk. It belongs to bijin-ga, a Japanese tradition of pictures of beautiful women, and the title names a woman from long ago in China. Look at the fine lines and the patterned robes. How do they show care and patience?
descriptions.g68: Yang Guifei (1922) is a silk painting in opaque watercolor by Uemura Shōen, a leading painter of bijin-ga. The title points to a figure from Tang-dynasty China, so the picture looks back to an older story through a twentieth-century Japanese eye. How do robes, pose and delicate color help the painter suggest a long-ago world?
descriptions.g910: Uemura Shōen's Yang Guifei (1922) shows how Nihonga artists used mineral-based pigments and silk to renew traditional subjects. The bijin-ga genre centers on women, and here a historical figure from China is imagined by a Japanese woman painter. How do surface, line and costume build an atmosphere that feels both historical and modern?
descriptions.g1112: Yang Guifei (1922) sits within Nihonga, the movement that shaped Japanese-style painting against Western-influenced oil painting, and within the bijin-ga tradition. Uemura Shōen was a woman working in a field long led by men, painting a Tang-dynasty figure known through poems and legends. How might you weigh the painting as portrait, as story and as statement of artistic identity?

k.daily: Look at her robes. Which colors and patterns do you like best?
k.emotion: How does her soft, quiet painting make you feel?
k.observation: Find her hair and her clothes. What do you see in each one?
k.analysis: Where does the woman sit or stand in the painting, and what is around her?
k.line: Trace one thin line in her robe with your finger. Where does it go?
k.shape: Find a big shape in her robes. What does it remind you of?
k.color: Which colors in Yang Guifei look gentle, and which look bright?
k.texture: Silk is smooth and shiny. How might this painting feel if you touched it?
k.space: Is the woman close to you or far away? What tells you?
k.light: Where do you see light colors, and where do you see darker ones?
k.meaning: Why do you think the painter chose to paint someone from a story?
k.culture: This painting comes from Japan. What would you tell a friend about it?
k.technique: The painter used watercolor on silk. How is that different from a crayon on paper?
k.personal: If you could wear one robe from this painting, which would you pick?
k.critical: What would you add to Yang Guifei if you could paint one more thing?

g12.daily: What tiny details in Yang Guifei's robes make you want to keep looking?
g12.emotion: What mood do you feel from this quiet silk painting, and what shows it?
g12.observation: Make a list of everything you see on her clothes, from her hair to her sleeves.
g12.analysis: Why does your eye move to the woman first instead of the edges of the painting?
g12.line: How do the thin, curving lines make her robes look like they are flowing?
g12.shape: Which round or flowing shapes do you find in her clothing, and which are straight?
g12.color: How do the soft colors in Yang Guifei make the painting feel calm?
g12.texture: How did the painter make cloth in a painting look soft and layered?
g12.space: How does the picture show where the woman stands compared with the background?
g12.light: Where does the light seem to touch her face and robes most?
g12.meaning: Why might the painter have chosen a woman from an old story for this picture?
g12.culture: What can robes in a painting like this teach us about how people dressed in Japan or China long ago?
g12.technique: Why might silk be a special surface to paint on instead of paper?
g12.personal: What would you want to ask the woman in this painting?
g12.critical: Why do you think the painter spent so much time on tiny details?

g35.daily: Which details of the robes and hair in Yang Guifei show how slowly and carefully Uemura Shōen worked?
g35.emotion: What feeling comes from her pose and expression, and which details support it?
g35.observation: Study the patterns on her clothing. How many different kinds can you find, and where do they repeat?
g35.analysis: How does the placement of the woman guide your eyes across the tall silk painting?
g35.line: How do the fine outlines in this bijin-ga picture differ from the brush lines in a rough sketch?
g35.shape: How do the large shapes of her robes create a main form that stands out from the rest of the painting?
g35.color: How do muted colors and a few brighter accents shape the mood of Yang Guifei?
g35.texture: How does the painter suggest the feel of layered silk cloth without actual folds you can touch?
g35.space: What clues show how much space the figure takes up, and how the picture keeps her central?
g35.light: How does the painter use light and dark colors to show shape in her robes?
g35.meaning: What might the painter want us to think about by choosing a famous woman from Tang China?
g35.culture: What does this painting suggest about how Japanese artists in 1922 looked back at older Chinese stories?
g35.technique: What do you think opaque watercolor on silk allows that oil paint on canvas does not?
g35.personal: What question would you ask Uemura Shōen about why she painted Yang Guifei?
g35.critical: Some people only see a pretty picture here. What evidence from the painting shows more skill and thought?

g68.daily: How do the fine lines and layered colors in Yang Guifei reward slow, close looking?
g68.emotion: Which choices of posture and color give the figure a mood that seems dignified rather than playful?
g68.observation: Compare the detail in the robes with the way the rest of the painting is treated. What differences stand out?
g68.analysis: How does the tall format and the placement of the figure organize your eyes from top to bottom?
g68.line: How do the flowing contours of the robes differ from the sharper edges where patterns meet?
g68.shape: How do the large curved masses of fabric build the silhouette of the figure?
g68.color: How does the restrained palette in this opaque watercolor affect the feeling of elegance?
g68.texture: How does the painter convey the quality of silk cloth and hair using only paint on a silk surface?
g68.space: How does the shallow space around the figure make her seem more like a symbol than a person in a real room?
g68.light: How does gentle, even light, with no strong shadows, change the mood compared with a dramatic oil painting?
g68.meaning: What might a modern painter be saying by showing a Tang-dynasty woman from legend in 1922?
g68.culture: How might ideas about beauty, history and gender in Japan in the early twentieth century shape a picture like this?
g68.technique: How does working in opaque watercolor on silk, a Nihonga method, influence the finish you see?
g68.personal: How would you describe the woman's personality using only visual evidence, and what would you leave uncertain?
g68.critical: Does a beautiful surface make a painting simple, or can beauty hold more complex ideas? Use details to explain.

g910.daily: Which painted details in Yang Guifei do the most to turn a decorative surface into a convincing presence?
g910.emotion: What emotional tone does the controlled, quiet handling of the figure create, and how do posture and color support it?
g910.observation: Examine the transition between sleeves, patterned fabric and background. What does the edge treatment reveal about the painter's method?
g910.analysis: How does the tall vertical format shape the way the figure's pose and costume are arranged and read?
g910.line: How do continuous, fine contours organize the complex patterns without making them feel stiff?
g910.shape: How do the flat, simplified shapes of the garments combine with detailed patterns to produce a layered design?
g910.color: How does the limited, harmonious palette unify the figure and the setting?
g910.texture: What does the silk support add to the quality of the surface compared with canvas or paper?
g910.space: How do shallow depth and the absence of strong perspective affect how the figure and background relate?
g910.light: How does soft, even illumination serve the painting's aims differently from dramatic chiaroscuro?
g910.meaning: What might the combination of a Chinese historical figure and a Japanese woman painter suggest about cultural exchange?
g910.culture: How does the bijin-ga tradition shape expectations about how women appear in pictures, and where might this work extend or question them?
g910.technique: How do the properties of opaque mineral-based pigment affect the appearance of color and edge compared with transparent washes?
g910.personal: What does the painting make you consider about how legendary figures are remembered through beauty rather than action?
g910.critical: To what extent is the idealization of the figure a limitation, and what could a critic say in the painting's defense?

g1112.daily: How does the combination of ornamental surface and inward restraint allow Yang Guifei to be read as portrait, legend and self-assertion at once?
g1112.emotion: Might the calm emotional register be a property of the figure or of the Nihonga conventions the painter works within? Weigh the visual evidence.
g1112.observation: Scan the junctions of garment pattern, skin and ground. How do the controlled boundaries shape your sense of the figure?
g1112.analysis: How does the vertical composition and the placement of the figure produce a sense of presence without a dramatic setting?
g1112.line: How does the economy and continuity of line in Yang Guifei relate to older East Asian traditions of figure painting?
g1112.shape: In what ways do the layered, patterned masses of the costume operate as abstract design as well as description?
g1112.color: How does the subdued, layered color serve a conception of elegance and what might it withhold?
g1112.texture: How does the tactile quality of mineral pigment on silk relate to ideas of craft and permanence in Nihonga?
g1112.space: How does the compressed, nearly flat space align the painting with decorative traditions rather than with Western perspective?
g1112.light: How does the even, shadowless light contribute to the idealized treatment of the sitter, and what does it exclude?
g1112.meaning: How does a twentieth-century Japanese woman painter's treatment of a Tang-dynasty figure complicate the genre of bijin-ga as an object of the male gaze?
g1112.culture: How do transnational stories, such as a Chinese court legend retold in Japanese painting, complicate the idea of a single national tradition?
g1112.technique: How does the commitment to Nihonga materials in 1922 respond to the rival prestige of oil painting, and what is gained or lost?
g1112.personal: How does your own cultural background shape what you expect from a picture of a woman from history, and does this painting meet or resist that expectation?
g1112.critical: What would a persuasive argument look like that Yang Guifei is more than a beautiful picture, and how would you test it against what is visible?

safety.method: Image viewed and approved by the site owner (visual review) on 2026-10-18. Earlier metadata screening: Title, medium (opaque watercolor on silk), year (1922), collection (Shōhaku Art Museum) and page tags (Women, Bijin-ga) read from the arthistoryproject.com page text; no concerning terms. The page labels the movement 'Meiji', which does not fit a 1922 work, so the accepted label Nihonga (bijin-ga tradition) is used instead. Only page text was read; the image file was not visually inspected, and a person should confirm it (figure clothed, no inappropriate content) before release.

teacherNote.context: A 1922 silk painting in opaque watercolor by Uemura Shōen, held by the Shōhaku Art Museum, in the bijin-ga tradition. The title names Yang Guifei, a famous woman from Tang-dynasty China.
directions: Have students list three patterns they find in the robes and sketch one, then discuss how repeated patterns guide the eye.
Ask students to compare drawing a figure on paper with a pencil and painting one on a smooth surface, and discuss what changes.
Invite a discussion of why painters return to older stories and how retelling can change them.
